chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him): 'Which hour do you prefer that I depart from Jamʿ (al-Muzdalifah)?' He said, 'A little before the sun rises; it is the most beloved of the hours to me.' I said, 'And if I stay until the sun rises?' He said, 'There is no harm in that.'

key_terms.أَفَّاضَ: To depart or move from a place, specifically referring to the departure from Muzdalifah
key_terms.جَمْع: Al-Jam', a name for Muzdalifah where pilgrims collect pebbles
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no harm in it (indicating validity/permissibility)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred time to leave Muzdalifah for Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the preference for departing al-Muzdalifah before sunrise highlights the concept of *istihbab* (recommended act) rather than obligation, distinguishing the optimal time from the permissible window. This flexibility underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease in ritual performance, allowing pilgrims to balance spiritual devotion with physical capacity. The hadith serves as a key reference for determining the precise timing of the *Ramy al-Jamarat* ritual at Mina.
